newsitem.title: USA: CME hog futures end higher, bellies mixed.
newsitem.headline: CME hog futures end higher, bellies mixed.

text.p: CME lean hog futures closed higher while pork bellies ended mixed, with hogs supported by talk meat packers may soon increase pork production in anticipation of exporting pork to Japan, traders said.
Pork bellies ended mixed with differing fundmentals pulling prices in two directions.
Hog futures traders relayed talk demand for hogs should increase in June because packers will need to build pork inventories ahead of Japan's expected removal of tariffs on imported pork.
"That had a lot to do with the buying here," said a floor broker for a cash-connected firm.
Japan is expected to remove the tariffs July 1.

That buying pushed July and August hog futures into buy-stops that accelerated gains and pushed July to a peak of 82.375 cents and August to 80.400. However, both months slipped from the highs by the close.
"In another week or so that whole process (stockpiling) will start," said one analyst of plans for Japanese sales.
Lower cash hog prices at Midwest markets Tuesday weighed on hog futures early, but traders later said cash hogs were expected to trade steady Wednesday.
Demand may increase Wednesday compared with Tuesday because packers need hogs for Saturday slaughter after the lack of production on Monday because of the Memorial Day holiday.
However, cash traders expect steady to $1.00 per lower cash hog prices Wednesday because some major packers have enough hogs for Wednesday's slaughter needs.

Pork belly futures closed mixed with early gains linked to support from thin supplies in storage. However, that buying was displaced by selling driven by sluggish retail demand for bacon made from the high-priced fresh bellies.
"It is a tug-o-war," said Bill Cipolla, a trader for Iowa Grain. "I think it will go up. There are still no bellies in the box (storage)."

USDA on May 20 reported there were 54.017 million lbs of frozen pork bellies in storage, down from 54.767 million a month earlier and from 57.174 million a year earlier. Analysts said the May figure was the second time on record that the May supply was less than April stocks.
Hogs closed up 0.925 cent per lb to down 0.300 cent with June up 0.550 at 81.200 cents. Pork bellies were up 0.125 to down 0.950 cent with July off 0.600 at 91.900.
